title: Stop DOM-mutation rescan from scrolling the viewport back to the active match
description: Oculist's MutationObserver-driven rescan called highlightActiveRange(false), which ran element.scrollIntoView(...) and yanked the viewport back to the active match whenever the page mutated (lazy-load, infinite scroll) while the user was scrolling elsewhere. Fix: added skipScroll parameter to highlightActiveRange, passed true from rescanAfterMutation, and gated the scroll branch on !skipScroll. Interactive navigation (typing search, prev/next, replay) is unaffected.

title: Add 4 elemental candidates (Round 5) to effects-playground.html
description:
Add a new 'Round 5' of 4 candidate effects to artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html — one per classical element (Fire, Water, Earth, Air) — following the exact conventions established by the existing 26 effects (Rounds 1-4) already in that file.

Read the file first, especially the Round 4 section (fxImpactburst, fxSpeedlines, fxShattercrack, fxHardfreeze near the end of the effect functions, and the effectsRegistry/buildSidebar code at the bottom) for the current shape of the conventions before writing anything.

Conventions to follow (same as every prior round):
- Effect = `function fxName(r) { ... }`, `r` is the shared `#match` element's rect.
- Every element you create gets `className` including `'fx'`, mounted via the existing `mount(el)` helper.
- Self-clean via your own `setTimeout` + `.remove()` — don't rely solely on `clearFx()` (that's the rapid-retrigger safety net, not your primary cleanup path).
- If an effect needs to temporarily mutate page-wide state (body transform, mark text color, etc.), capture/restore it via `addRestorer`/`removeRestorer` (see fxGravity or fxZoompunch for the pattern). Prefer not mutating page-wide state at all unless the effect genuinely needs it.
- Naming: function `fxCapitalizedsquashedname` (e.g. `fxImpactburst`, `fxHardfreeze` — capitalize only the first letter, no inner camelCase), registry key = same name lowercased with no `fx` prefix.
- Register all 4 in `effectsRegistry` after the existing 26 entries, in the same `{ label: '...', run: fxWhatever }` shape.
- Extend `buildSidebar()`'s round-slicing so a 'Round 5' divider appears after 'Round 4', containing exactly these 4, using `addDivider('Round 5', round5)` after the existing `addDivider('Round 4', round4)` call — don't change how rounds 1-4 are computed/labeled.
- Use the existing `Z` constant (2147483645) for z-index, same as every other effect.
- No autoplay on load — fires only via sidebar button click or 'Replay last', same as all existing effects.

IMPORTANT DEPARTURE from Round 4's design language: Round 4 effects were deliberately short (~150-350ms) and hard-edged/flat-colored to read as anime 'impact frames'. These 4 elemental effects should NOT follow that template — each should move at whatever pace and visual texture suits its element, per the approved design below. Some will run longer and softer than anything in Round 4, and that's intentional, not a bug.

Build these 4, per the approved design:

1. **Fire — "Ember Ignite"** (`fxEmberignite` / key `emberignite`) — total runtime ~700ms. A flame-silhouette shape (e.g. a rounded teardrop/blob built with border-radius or clip-path) rises from the match, with a warm gradient from deep red at the base to yellow/white at the tip. Flicker the flame's opacity and a slight horizontal skew/scaleX across 2-3 short cycles during its life (not a single smooth animate — genuinely wobble, e.g. via multiple keyframes with alternating small offsets) so it reads as an unstable flame rather than a static glowing shape. Also emit 3-4 small ember/spark particles that drift upward with slight horizontal drift (not perfectly straight), shrinking and fading as they rise. Soft/glowing edges (box-shadow or blur-ish gradient), not flat — fire should look hot.

2. **Water — "Ripple Surge"** (`fxRipplesurge` / key `ripplesurge`) — total runtime ~1000ms. 2-3 concentric ring outlines (border-radius circles, transparent fill, colored border) expand outward from the match center on an ease-out curve (fast start, decelerating, like a real ripple), fading opacity as they grow, staggered slightly so they don't perfectly overlap. Also one droplet element that arcs upward from the match then falls back with a small bounce/settle at the end (a simple 2-phase animation: rise+fall via a parabolic-feeling easing, then a quick small bounce). Translucent blue/cyan, soft edges — water should look wet and fluid, not solid.

3. **Earth — "Rockfall Thud"** (`fxRockfallthud` / key `rockfallthud`) — total runtime ~650ms (~120ms hard impact phase, ~500ms settle phase). Start with a quick heavy 'impact' cue: a brief sharp downward jolt on a small area around the match (e.g. a fast translateY snap-down-then-up on a couple of rock-shard elements, or a very brief page-local shake if you want, but keep any page-wide mutation properly restored via addRestorer if you use one — a self-contained local jolt on your own new elements is simpler and preferred). Then 4-6 angular rock/debris shard fragments (small irregular polygons via clip-path, or simple rotated rectangles/triangles) pop outward and arc back down under a gravity-like ease-in fall, settling near the ground line. Also a low dust-puff cloud (1-2 soft low-opacity flattened ellipses) expanding and fading at the base. Matte, mostly-opaque earthy colors (browns/grays), minimal glow — earth should feel heavy and solid, not glowy.

4. **Air — "Gust Swirl"** (`fxGustswirl` / key `gustswirl`) — total runtime ~600ms. 2-3 thin curved wind-streak strokes (e.g. thin elongated divs with border-radius to fake a curve, or a small set of short rotated segments approximating a curve) swirl around the match in a spiral/orbit-like path and drift off past its edges, fading as they exit. Add 1-2 small drifting particles (tiny dots/dashes) caught in the current, moving along a gentle curved path. Pale, low-opacity, thin/wispy — air should feel light and barely-there, not solid or saturated.

Colors (keep each element visually unambiguous from the others and from all prior rounds):
- Fire: warm red-to-yellow gradient (e.g. base `#dc2626`/`#b91c1c` to tip `#facc15`/`#fde047`)
- Water: blue/cyan (e.g. `#0ea5e9` or `#06b6d4`), translucent
- Earth: brown/stone gray (e.g. `#78716c` or `#92400e`), mostly opaque
- Air: pale gray-white or very light blue (e.g. `#e2e8f0` or `#f1f5f9`), low opacity throughout

Edge cases:
- Each effect must be independently replayable in rapid succession without leaking elements (same standard as every prior round) — verify `.fx` count returns to its pre-fire baseline after each effect's own cleanup timeout, not just relying on clearFx().
- Don't reuse colors across the 4 elements in a way that makes them hard to tell apart.
- No new dependencies, no build step — this file stays a single self-contained HTML file like it already is.

Verification (no test suite exists for this prototype file):
- Load the file in a browser (this repo's playwright devDependency works for a scripted check), click each of the 4 new Round 5 sidebar buttons, confirm zero console errors, confirm each effect visibly does something distinct from the others (sample computed opacity/transform mid-animation for at least the flame flicker and the ripple rings to confirm they're actually animating, not just present in the DOM), and confirm `.fx` node count returns to baseline within ~1.5s of each firing.
- Spot-check 2 pre-existing effects from different earlier rounds (e.g. Sonar Ping from Round 1, Impact Burst from Round 4) still fire correctly and Round 1-4 grouping is untouched.
- No changes to any file outside artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.
acceptance_criteria: 4 new effects (emberignite, ripplesurge, rockfallthud, gustswirl) registered in effectsRegistry and grouped under a new 'Round 5' sidebar divider; each fires via its sidebar button with zero console errors, visibly animates (not just a static flash), and self-cleans its .fx nodes within ~1.5s; existing 26 effects and Round 1-4 grouping unaffected; no changes outside effects-playground.html
close_reason: Round 5 (Ember Ignite, Ripple Surge, Rockfall Thud, Gust Swirl) added to effects-playground.html; reviewer-verified, plus a fix pass for Gust Swirl's low contrast and Earth's abrupt jolt-shard pop-out. No changes outside the playground file.

title: Honour OS-level prefers-reduced-motion when choosing beacon motion
description:
Oculist honours its own motionSensitivity setting (visionSettings.motionSensitivity: full | reduced | off) but never checks the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion media query. A user who has asked their operating system to reduce motion still gets full beacon animations unless they separately find and change the extension setting.

Original scope also covered capping flash opacity on the Impact Burst / Speed Lines effects; those effects were reverted in 2554612 and 1b9f7de, so that half no longer applies (see closed oculist-kd7).

Remaining work: treat window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') as a downgrade-only signal on the motion mode read in content.js — drawActiveOverlays() (~1567) and animate() (~1607) both compute the same value. When the OS asks for reduced motion, 'full' becomes 'reduced'; an explicit 'reduced' or 'off' is left alone, so the setting can only ever reduce motion further, never override the OS upward. Must react to the media query changing at runtime, not just at load.
close_reason: Implemented in 0f89a22 on branch v1.6.0. Shared effectiveMotion() in extension/content.js downgrades 'full' to 'reduced' when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') matches; explicit 'reduced'/'off' untouched. Regression test test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js flips the emulated preference at runtime and asserts the beacon part count drops and restores; verified it fails without the fix. Full suite: 22/22 pass.

title: Add 4 impact-frame candidates (Round 4) to effects-playground.html
description:
CORRECTION to original brief: artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html already exists (predates this epic) as a living gallery of 22 candidate beacon effects across 'Round 1/2/3', built specifically for this kind of side-by-side prototyping. Do NOT create a new file or a new grid/card layout — extend this existing file with a new 'Round 4' of 4 additional candidates, following its established conventions exactly.

Existing conventions to match (read the file first, don't guess):
- Effects are `function fxName(r) { ... }`, where `r` is the single shared `#match` element's rect (one real article, one real `<mark id="match">`, not per-candidate cards).
- Elements you create get `className` including `'fx'` (see existing fx* functions for the exact pattern) and are mounted via the existing `mount(el)` helper (appends to document.documentElement).
- Only one effect is 'live' at a time: `window.runEffect(key)` calls `clearFx()` first (removes all `.fx` nodes and drains any registered restorers), then `eff.run(rect())`. Don't fight this — build your 4 effects to be self-cleaning within their own duration like the existing ones (most use a `setTimeout` to remove their own elements), the `clearFx()` safety net is for rapid re-trigger, not your primary cleanup path.
- If an effect temporarily mutates page state outside its own new elements (e.g. body transform, mark text color), capture prior state and register a restorer via `addRestorer(fn)`, following the `captureStyleAttr`/`restoreStyleAttr` pattern already in the file (search for `addRestorer` usage in an existing effect, e.g. fxGravity or fxZoompunch, for a concrete example). Prefer NOT mutating page-wide state at all if your effect doesn't need to — simpler is fine here.
- Naming convention: function `fxCapitalizedsquashedname` (e.g. `fxZoompunch`, `fxDepthdive`, `fxMatchstrike` — capitalize only the first letter, rest of the compound name is lowercase, no inner camelCase), registry key is the same name lowercased with no prefix (e.g. `zoompunch`, `depthdive`).
- Registration: add 4 new entries to the `effectsRegistry` object (around line 1514) AFTER the existing 22, in the same `{ label: '...', run: fxWhatever }` shape.
- Sidebar grouping: `buildSidebar()` currently slices `window.EFFECTS` into round1 (first 10, no divider), round2 (next 5, 'Round 2' divider), round3 (remainder, 'Round 3' divider). Add a 'Round 4' divider for your 4 new entries — extend the slicing logic (e.g. `window.EFFECTS.slice(15, 19)` for round3 and `.slice(19)` for a new round4, or whatever indices are correct given the final registry order) and call `addDivider('Round 4', round4)` after the existing `addDivider('Round 3', round3)` call. Do not change how rounds 1-3 are computed/labeled.
- Use the `Z` constant (2147483645) for any z-index, matching every existing effect.
- No autoplay on load — effects only fire via sidebar button click or the 'Replay last' button, exactly like the existing 22. Do not add a load-time autoplay for your 4.

Design intent (why these 4, and why they should look distinct from a generic 'glowing highlight'): these are 'impact frame' candidates, inspired by anime/manga impact-frame conventions — hard, SHORT, high-contrast hits rather than smooth glowing animations. Aim for roughly 150-350ms total runtime per effect (a handful of anime frames), near-instant snaps rather than long eased curves, and flat/hard-edged shapes (solid fills, bold outlines) rather than soft blurred gradients. This is a deliberate contrast with most of the existing 22 effects, which tend to be smoother/longer — that contrast is the point of this round.

Build these 4:
1. **Impact Burst** (`fxImpactburst` / key `impactburst`) — hard white flash (~60-80ms) + a flat-color jagged star/burst shape centered on the match that snaps to full size almost instantly and cuts off abruptly (no long fade).
2. **Speed Lines** (`fxSpeedlines` / key `speedlines`) — flat-color (not gradient) straight lines radiating from the match at evenly-spaced angles, snapping to full length fast, hard cutoff.
3. **Shatter Crack** (`fxShattercrack` / key `shattercrack`) — 8-14 jagged 2-segment 'crack' lines at randomized angles/lengths radiating from the match (mimicking a glass-crack impact), plus a quick flash. Each 'crack' = two short connected line segments at a slight angle offset, not a single straight line (that's what makes it read as a crack rather than a ray).
4. **Hard Freeze Flash** (`fxHardfreeze` / key `hardfreeze`) — the most literal 'impact frame': a near-full-opacity flash across the viewport for ~2-3 frames (~80-120ms), plus a bold angular outline that snaps around the match at the same instant. Prefer `steps()` or a very short easing over long cubic-bezier curves.

Verification (no test suite exists for this file — it's a prototype):
- Open the file in a browser (this repo's playwright devDependency works fine for a scripted check) and click each of the 4 new sidebar buttons; confirm zero console errors, each effect visibly fires near the match, and `.fx` node count returns to its pre-fire baseline within ~1s of each firing (no leaks).
- Confirm the existing 22 effects and their Round 1/2/3 grouping are untouched and still work (spot-check a couple, e.g. click 'Sonar Ping' and 'Ink Bloom').
- No changes to any file outside artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.
acceptance_criteria: 4 new effects (impactburst, speedlines, shattercrack, hardfreeze) registered in effectsRegistry and grouped under a new 'Round 4' sidebar divider; each fires via its sidebar button with zero console errors and self-cleans its .fx nodes within ~1s; existing 22 effects and Round 1/2/3 grouping unaffected; no changes outside effects-playground.html
close_reason: Round 4 (Impact Burst, Speed Lines, Shatter Crack, Hard Freeze Flash) added to effects-playground.html; reviewer-verified after 2 rounds of fixes (options-level steps() misuse, burst-point clamping, keyframe fade-back artifact). No changes outside the playground file.

title: Add 'Speed Lines' effect (manga radiating focus lines + hitstop)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js mimicking manga/anime 'speed lines' (a.k.a. focus lines): straight lines radiating from the impact point across a wide radius, evoking the classic manga panel technique used at a moment of impact, combined with a brief hitstop flash.

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectSpeedLines: 'Speed Lines'` near the other `effect*` keys.
2. Write `function animateSpeedLines(rect) { ... }`, placed near the other `animate*` effect functions. Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;`.
3. Visual composition, `position:fixed` (viewport-anchored, same convention as `animateIris` at content.js:466):
   a. A brief hitstop flash: full-viewport white overlay, opacity spikes 0 -> ~0.5 -> 0 fast (~100-150ms), lower peak opacity than a full flash effect since the lines carry most of the visual weight here.
   b. 12-20 thin straight lines radiating outward from the match center at evenly distributed angles (`360 / count` degrees apart), each a rotated absolutely-positioned div (`width: 1-3px scaled by getBeaconScale()`, long length e.g. 40-60% of viewport diagonal, `transform-origin` at the near end so it grows outward from the match like a manga speed line). Animate each line's length via `transform: scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1) -> scaleX(0.3)` (grows fast, recedes) with a fast easing, staggered fade-out.
   c. Color: use `getEffectiveColors().beacon` for the lines (see note below on accessibility), optionally blended with white near the origin for a 'hot core' look, consistent with how `animateAnimeLaser` mixes accent color + white (content.js:380-400).
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'`.
5. Color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon` as the primary driver, not hardcoded black/white-only — this project's Vision Accessibility Suite depends on every effect reflecting the user's active beacon color for color-blind palette support, so don't design a monochrome-only variant even though real manga speed lines are typically black ink on white.
6. Scale line length/width/count by `getBeaconScale()`; reduce line count under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same pattern as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end, not incrementally.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`.
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `speedlines: { label: i18n.effectSpeedLines, run: animateSpeedLines },`. Do not reorder or touch other entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op.
- Keep this visually distinct from the sibling 'Impact Burst' task (star-shaped burst) — this effect is straight uniform radiating lines, not a star polygon. If both tasks land, they should not look like near-duplicates.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-order and effect-existence assertions.
- 'Speed Lines' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list.
- Triggering the effect creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing.
- No files changed outside repo/extension/content.js.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Speed Lines' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); visually distinct from the Impact Burst star shape; no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Speed Lines effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks, visually distinct from Impact Burst.

title: Add 'Impact Burst' effect (comic star-burst impact frame)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js that mimics an anime/manga 'impact frame': a hard white flash + a jagged comic-style star burst snapping onto the active match, evoking a punch/hit moment (reference: anime impact frames — hard cut to white/flash, sharp radiating burst shape, brief hitstop, then release).

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectImpactBurst: 'Impact Burst'` alongside the other `effect*` keys (near line 177).
2. Write `function animateImpactBurst(rect) { ... }` placed near the other `animate*` effect functions (e.g. after `animateAnimeLaser` at content.js:324 or `animateIris` at content.js:466 — follow whichever sibling function's structure is closest). Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;` (copy this exact pattern from animateAnimeLaser).
3. Visual composition (three layered elements, all `position:fixed` since the effect is viewport-anchored on the match, same convention as `animateIris`):
   a. A brief full-viewport white flash overlay (inset 0) that spikes opacity 0 -> ~0.85 -> 0 very fast (~100-150ms total) to simulate a 'hitstop' flash-cut. Use `getBeaconDuration(...)` for all durations, never a raw literal.
   b. A jagged star-burst shape centered on `rect` (use `clip-path: polygon(...)` with 8-12 alternating long/short points to fake a comic impact star), filled with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, sized relative to `rect` and `getBeaconScale()`. Animate transform scale with an overshoot easing (e.g. `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) so it 'snaps' in rather than eases smoothly — 0.2 -> 1.3 -> 1, then fades.
   c. 6-10 short radiating spike lines around the match (thin rotated divs, angle evenly distributed like a starburst), colored with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, scaling outward and fading — reuse the randomized-placement-loop pattern from the spark generation in `animateAnimeLaser` (content.js:428-456) for consistency, but evenly spaced angles instead of random (bursts read as more 'impact', sparks read as more 'explosion').
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'` (required for the extension's cleanup/resize/DOM-scan logic — grep `.oc-beacon` usage in content.js to confirm all touchpoints before finishing).
5. Color: primary visual color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, not a hardcoded black/white-only palette — this project has a Vision Accessibility Suite with color-blind palettes that depend on every effect surfacing the user's active beacon color, so don't design an effect that reads correctly only in one color scheme. White is fine for flash/highlight accents (other effects mix white + accent color), just not as the *only* color.
6. Scale all counts/sizes by `getBeaconScale()`, and downscale element/spike counts under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` logic (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end (not incrementally) to avoid layout thrashing, per the existing comment convention in `animateAnimeLaser`.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element created by this effect, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`, mirroring `animateIris`'s multi-element cleanup (content.js:521-524).
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `burst: { label: i18n.effectImpactBurst, run: animateImpactBurst },`. Do not reorder or touch the other 7 entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, the settings-panel sort logic, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op (return early), same as all sibling effects.
- Must not throw if called back-to-back rapidly (user pressing next-match fast) — rely on the same fire-and-forget DOM node pattern the other effects use; do not add any global mutable state beyond what's local to the function call.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` (repo/package.json → `node --test test/*.test.js`) passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-label-order assertion and existing effect-existence assertions.
- 'Impact Burst' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list (auto-sorted alphabetically by the existing code — no manual sort-order edit needed).
- Manually triggering the effect (e.g. via the extension's find bar on a page, or a quick jsdom/script smoke check) creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all of which are removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing (no leaked nodes).
- No changes outside `repo/extension/content.js`.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Impact Burst' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and on a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Impact Burst effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks.

title: Fix clipped box-shadow glow on Impact Burst effect
description: In repo/extension/content.js, animateImpactBurst()'s burst-shape element has both clip-path (for the star polygon) and box-shadow (for glow) — clip-path clips box-shadow, so the glow never renders. Move the glow to a separate unclipped element behind the star, or drop the box-shadow. Cosmetic only, found during review of oculist-y9h.1.
